## Overview

The United States of America (USA), also known as the United States (U.S.) or America, is a country primarily located 
in North America. It is a federal republic of 50 states and a federal capital district, Washington, D.C. 


The 48 contiguous states border Canada to the north and Mexico to the south, with the semi-exclave of Alaska in 
the northwest and the archipelago of Hawaii in the Pacific Ocean. The United States also asserts sovereignty over 
five major island territories and various uninhabited islands in Oceania and the Caribbean. It is a megadiverse country, 
with the world's third-largest land area and third-largest population, exceeding 340 million.

## History

The Mayflower Compact in Massachusetts and the Fundamental Orders of Connecticut established precedents for 
representative self-governance and constitutionalism that would develop throughout the American colonies. While 
European settlers in what is now the United States experienced conflicts with Native Americans, they also engaged 
in trade, exchanging European tools for food and animal pelts. Relations ranged from close cooperation to warfare 
and massacres. The colonial authorities often pursued policies that forced Native Americans to adopt European 
lifestyles, including conversion to Christianity.

In 1776, the thirteen American colonies declared independence from British rule. The country has since grown to 
become the world's largest economy and one of the most powerful nations in the world.

## Economy

The United States has a highly developed diversified mixed economy. It is the world's largest economy by 
nominal GDP and second largest by purchasing power parity (PPP). As of 2025, it has the world's seventh 
highest nominal GDP per capita and ninth highest GDP per capita by PPP. According to the World Bank, the U.S. 
accounted for 14.8% of the global aggregate GDP in 2024 in purchasing power parity terms and 26.2% in 
nominal terms. The U.S. dollar is the currency of record most used in international transactions and is 
the world's foremost reserve currency, backed by a large U.S. treasuries market, its role as the reference 
standard for the petrodollar system, and its linked eurodollar. Several countries use it as their official 
currency and in others it is the de facto currency. Since the end of World War II, the economy has achieved 
relatively steady growth, low unemployment and inflation, and rapid advances in technology.

## Overview

George Washington (February 22, 1732 to December 14, 1799) was the first president of the United States,
serving from 1789 to 1797. He led the Continental Army to victory in the American Revolutionary War,
presided over the Constitutional Convention of 1787, and established many important precedents for the
national government and presidency.

## Legacy

In surveys of U.S. scholars ranking presidents since 1948, the top three presidents are generally Lincoln,
George Washington, and Franklin Delano Roosevelt, although the order varies. Washington is consistently
ranked among the top three presidents in both academic and public opinion polls. His leadership during
the Revolutionary War, role in founding the republic, and establishment of key presidential precedents
have earned him the informal title "Father of His Country."

## Overview

Abraham Lincoln (February 12, 1809 to April 15, 1865) was the 16th president of the United States, 
serving from 1861 until his assassination in 1865. He led the United States through the American Civil War, 
defeating the Confederate States of America and playing a major role in the abolition of slavery.

## Legacy

In surveys of U.S. scholars ranking presidents since 1948, the top three presidents are generally Lincoln, 
George Washington, and Franklin Delano Roosevelt, although the order varies. Between 1999 and 2011, 
Lincoln, John F. Kennedy, and Ronald Reagan were the top-ranked presidents in eight public opinion surveys 
by Gallup. A 2004 study found that scholars in history and politics ranked Lincoln number one, while legal 
scholars placed him second after Washington.

## Overview

Franklin Delano Roosevelt (January 30, 1882 to April 12, 1945) was the 32nd president of the United States,
serving from 1933 to 1945. He led the United States through the Great Depression and World War II,
implementing his New Deal domestic agenda in response to the worst economic crisis in U.S. history,
and forging the Allied Powers coalition that defeated Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan.

## Legacy

In surveys of U.S. scholars ranking presidents since 1948, the top three presidents are generally Lincoln,
George Washington, and Franklin Delano Roosevelt, although the order varies. Roosevelt is consistently
ranked among the top three presidents in both academic and public opinion polls. His leadership during
the Great Depression, World War II, and implementation of lasting New Deal programs like Social Security
have earned him recognition as one of America's greatest presidents.

## Overview

Pan and Pfeil (2004) count 87 distinct "peoples of Europe", of which 33 form the majority population in at 
least one sovereign state, while the remaining 54 constitute ethnic minorities. Romani people are the largest 
ethnic minority in Europe, according to European Commission.

## Trends

### Migration

Europe is home to the highest number of migrants of all global regions at nearly 87 million people in 2020, 
according to the International Organisation for Migration. In 2005, the EU had an overall net gain from 
immigration of 1.8 million people.

This accounted for almost 85% of Europe's total population growth. In 2021, 
827,000 persons were given citizenship of an EU member state, an increase of about 14% compared with 2020. 
2.3 million immigrants from non-EU countries entered the EU in 2021.

### Emigration

Early modern emigration from Europe began with Spanish and Portuguese settlers in the 16th century, and French 
and English settlers in the 17th century. But numbers remained relatively small until waves of mass emigration 
in the 19th century, when millions of poor families left Europe.

## Overview

Austria is a landlocked country in Central Europe, known for its rich cultural heritage, stunning Alpine 
landscapes, and historical significance. The country shares borders with Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, 
Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein. Its capital and largest city is Vienna, which served 
as the heart of the Habsburg Empire for centuries.

## Culture

Austrian culture is deeply rooted in the arts, particularly classical music, with famous composers like Mozart, 
Beethoven, and Strauss having strong connections to Vienna. The country is also renowned for its architectural 
heritage, featuring baroque buildings, imperial palaces, and medieval castles. Austrian cuisine, including 
dishes like Wiener Schnitzel and Sachertorte, reflects influences from its historical position at the crossroads of 
Central Europe.

## Overview

Italy is a country in Southern Europe, known for its rich cultural heritage, stunning Mediterranean 
landscapes, and historical significance. The country shares borders with France, Switzerland, Austria, 
Slovenia, and includes the enclaved microstates of Vatican City and San Marino. Its capital and largest 
city is Rome, which served as the heart of the Roman Empire and remains a major cultural center.

## Culture

Italian culture is deeply rooted in the arts, particularly Renaissance art and architecture, with famous artists 
like Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Botticelli. The country is also renowned for its architectural 
heritage, featuring ancient Roman ruins, Renaissance palaces, and medieval towns. Italian cuisine, including 
dishes like pasta, pizza, and gelato, has influenced culinary traditions worldwide and reflects the country's 
diverse regional cultures and Mediterranean heritage.

## Overview

Italy is a country in Southern Europe, known for its rich cultural heritage, stunning Mediterranean 
landscapes, and historical significance. The country shares borders with France, Switzerland, Austria, 
Slovenia, and includes the enclaved microstates of Vatican City and San Marino. Its capital and largest 
city is Rome, which served as the heart of the Roman Empire and remains a major cultural center.

## Culture

Italian culture is deeply rooted in the arts, particularly Renaissance art and architecture, with famous artists 
like Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Botticelli. The country is also renowned for its architectural 
heritage, featuring ancient Roman ruins, Renaissance palaces, and medieval towns. Italian cuisine, including 
dishes like pasta, pizza, and gelato, has influenced culinary traditions worldwide and reflects the country's 
diverse regional cultures and Mediterranean heritage.

## Overview

Switzerland is a landlocked country in Central Europe, known for its stunning Alpine landscapes, political 
neutrality, and high standard of living. The country shares borders with Germany, France, Italy, Austria, 
and Liechtenstein. Its capital is Bern, while Zürich is its largest city. Switzerland is renowned for its 
direct democracy system and has maintained a policy of armed neutrality since the 16th century.

## Culture

Swiss culture is a unique blend of German, French, Italian, and Romansh influences, reflecting its 
multilingual heritage. The country is famous for its precision watchmaking, banking sector, and culinary 
traditions including Swiss chocolate, cheese fondue, and raclette. Switzerland's cultural landscape includes 
picturesque mountain villages, medieval towns, and modern cities. The Swiss are known for their strong 
emphasis on quality, efficiency, and environmental consciousness.

## Claude Monet

Claude Monet was a French painter and a founder of Impressionism. He is most famous for his series of paintings 
depicting urban scenes, landscapes, and water lilies.

## Biography

Monet was born on November 14, 1840, in Paris, France. He was the son of a merchant and started painting at a young age. 
He studied at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris, where he was influenced by the works of Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot and 
Eugène Delacroix. He later became a member of the Impressionist movement, which he co-founded with artists like Pierre-Auguste 
Renoir, Alfred Sisley, and Berthe Morisot.

## Artistic Style

Monet's artistic style is characterized by his use of light and color to capture the fleeting effects of light and atmosphere. 
He is known for his loose brushstrokes and his ability to capture the changing effects of light on his subjects.

## Notable Works

Monet's most famous works include "Impression, Sunrise", "Water Lilies", and "Nympheas".

attributes.title: Search events
attributes.chunk: Search events (GET /events/search): Search historical events using time period, tags, or keywords. This endpoint accepts period, tags, and q as parameters. It returns A list of events matching the search criteria (200).
attributes.document:
# Search events

GET https://api.historylibrary.dev/v1/events/search

Search historical events using time period, tags, or keywords.

Reference: https://sandbox/history/api-reference/api-reference/event/search-events

## OpenAPI Specification

```yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: API
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /events/search:
    get:
      operationId: search-events
      summary: Search events
      description: Search historical events using time period, tags, or keywords.
      tags:
        - subpackage_event
      parameters:
        - name: period
          in: query
          description: Time period filter (e.g., "Renaissance", "World War II").
          required: false
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: tags
          in: query
          description: Comma-separated tags to filter (e.g., "art,science").
          required: false
          schema:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
        - name: q
          in: query
          description: Keyword search.
          required: false
          schema:
            type: string
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A list of events matching the search criteria
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/EventSummary'
servers:
  - url: https://api.historylibrary.dev/v1
components:
  schemas:
    EventSummary:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
        title:
          type: string
        period:
          type: string
        tags:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
      title: EventSummary

```

attributes.title: Get event by ID
attributes.chunk: Get event by ID (GET /events/{eventId}): Retrieve details about a historical event. This endpoint accepts eventId as parameters. It returns id, title, description, period, tags, and sources (200).
attributes.document:
# Get event by ID

GET https://api.historylibrary.dev/v1/events/{eventId}

Retrieve details about a historical event.

Reference: https://sandbox/history/api-reference/api-reference/event/get-event-by-id

## OpenAPI Specification

```yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: API
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /events/{eventId}:
    get:
      operationId: get-event-by-id
      summary: Get event by ID
      description: Retrieve details about a historical event.
      tags:
        - subpackage_event
      parameters:
        - name: eventId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: integer
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Event details retrieved successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Event'
servers:
  - url: https://api.historylibrary.dev/v1
components:
  schemas:
    Event:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
        title:
          type: string
        description:
          type: string
        period:
          type: string
        tags:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
        sources:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
      title: Event

```
